item.title: Retrieval as Navigation: DecisionRAG Asks a Tree Instead of Scoring a Corpus
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. The bottleneck in retrieval is not the size of the candidate pool. It is what you let the model see, and in which order. DecisionRAG replaces scoring with asking, and returns a 65.4 top-1 hit over 2.68M passages in 1.7 seconds. It also loses three cells, plainly. English voiceover, 3 minutes 12 seconds.

item.title: Allegedly the singularity has begun: three sums from an old-fashioned man
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: allegedly we are already inside the singularity. I will not argue about the word. I want to redo the three sums the argument rests on — who writes the code, how cheap intelligence has become, and what is left in the human column. A note on method: this is a reading note.

item.title: The Vector Database Landscape: An In-Depth Analysis of Architectures, Technologies, and Strategic Applications
item.description: tap to enlarge Section 1: The Rise of Vector Databases in the AI Era# 1.1 Beyond Traditional Databases: The Unstructured Data Challenge# The landscape of data management is undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by the proliferation of artificial intelligence and machine learning. For decades, the dominant paradigm has been the relational database, which excels at storing and querying structured data—information neatly organized into tables, rows, and columns with a predefined schema.
